assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, including dimension zero; H:E→E is a real linear map. For all v,w, inner(Hv,w)=inner(v,Hw). No supplied eigenbasis or commuting/certified H-square condition is assumed.

kappa>=1, alpha=1/(2kappa); for every v, alpha||v||²<=inner(v,Hv)<=||v||². These are the actual source symmetric operator bounds. Construction of H from genuine positive integral momentum weights belongs to Lemma4.6 and remains separate.
x,p range over all E, without probability laws, moment, measure, smoothness or integrability assumptions. The phase norm is the actual M_kappa quadratic form, not the default product max norm.
units.statement: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product E, kappa>=1, symmetric real linear H with (2kappa)^-1 I<=H<=I and every x,p∈E, D_H(x,p)>=Q_kappa(x,p)/(8kappa), where Q_kappa=(1/(2kappa)+1/2)||x||²+inner(x,p)+||p||² and D_H=inner(x,Hx)+2inner(p,Hx)-kappa^-1 inner(x,p)+||p||². With A_H(x,p)=(p,-Hx-p), M_kappa(x,p)=((alpha+1/2)x+p/2,x/2+p), this is exactly -2 inner(M_kappa(x,p),A_H(x,p))>=Q_kappa/(8kappa), hence the full matrix quadratic inequality (4.15). Product inner here is the sum of the two E inner products.

steps.title: Retain the actual two block operators
steps.text: Put alpha=1/(2kappa)∈(0,1/2]. The real full phase form is Q=(alpha+1/2)||x||²+inner(x,p)+||p||². Direct block multiplication for A_H(x,p)=(p,-Hx-p) and M_kappa gives -2 inner(M_kappa z,A_H z)=D_H. Source operator order is precisely comparison of these forms for every phase vector; no stochastic kernel contraction enters.
steps.formula: Q_\kappa=(\alpha+\tfrac12)\|x\|^2+\langle x,p\rangle+\|p\|^2,\quad D_H=\langle x,Hx\rangle+2\langle p,Hx\rangle-2\alpha\langle x,p\rangle+\|p\|^2.

steps.title: Prove the source scalar determinant lower bound
steps.text: For an eigenvalue alpha<=lambda<=1, factor lambda-(lambda-alpha)²-alpha=(lambda-alpha)(1+alpha-lambda)>=0. For t=1-alpha/2>0, det(([[lambda,lambda-alpha],[lambda-alpha,1]])-(alpha/2)I)>=0: its determinant is at least alpha(1-lambda)/2+alpha²/4. This exposes the PSD detail behind the source determinant/trace argument.

steps.title: Establish actual scalar coercivity
steps.text: Complete the square: t[(lambda-alpha/2)u²+2(lambda-alpha)uv+t v²]=(t v+(lambda-alpha)u)²+det*u²>=0. Hence D_lambda>=alpha(u²+v²)/2. Since alpha<=1/2 and (u-v)²>=0, the source M form is <=2(u²+v²). Thus D_lambda>=alpha Q_lambda/4, the exact source1/(8kappa) factor.

steps.title: Derive rather than assume the eigenvalue bounds
steps.text: Pinned Mathlib supplies an orthonormal eigenbasis b_i of the real symmetric H. At a unit basis vector, the actual full-space lower/upper quadratic hypotheses and H b_i=lambda_i b_i give alpha<=lambda_i<=1. The basis is internally obtained; no external certificate is supplied. Symmetry yields inner(b_i,Hx)=inner(Hb_i,x)=lambda_i inner(b_i,x).

steps.title: Lift every scalar block to the whole E
steps.text: Write u_i=inner(b_i,x),v_i=inner(b_i,p). Parseval and the exact inner-product sum identify sum u_i²=||x||², sum v_i²=||p||², sum u_i v_i=inner(x,p), sum lambda_i u_i²=inner(x,Hx) and sum lambda_i u_i v_i=inner(p,Hx). Sum the scalar inequalities and substitute all identities; this includes dimension zero without a nonempty basis hypothesis.

steps.title: Recover the precise source constant
steps.text: Use kappa>=1 to derive 0<alpha<=1/2. Substitute alpha=1/(2kappa), alpha/4=1/(8kappa),2alpha=1/kappa into the full-E inequality. Only the public source theorem receives admission; its two private proof helpers remain implementation details.
